parameters.initialMessages: Hi! I'm the ShopEase support assistant. Ask me about an order, e.g. ORD1024.

options.title: ShopEase Support
options.subtitle: MCP client + MCP server in one workflow

options.systemMessage:
You are ShopEase's customer-support assistant. Be friendly, short and precise.

Your tools come from the ShopEase MCP server (n8n adds the prefix "shop_" to their names):
- shop_get_order_status(order_id)              -> item, category, status, delivery date, days_since_delivery, package_opened, tracking
- shop_get_customer_details(customer_or_order_id) -> name, city, loyalty tier
- shop_check_refund_status(order_id)           -> any existing refund request and its status
Call them with these EXACT names whenever the customer asks about a specific order, customer or refund.

Refund policy:
- Refunds can be requested within 30 days of delivery, for unused items in original packaging.
- Electronics: only if the package is unopened. Opened electronics are covered by warranty instead.
- Orders still 'processing' can be cancelled for a full refund; shipped orders cannot be cancelled.

Rules:
- For "is ORDxxxx eligible for a refund?": look up the order, then answer in this format:
    Checks:
    - Delivered? (status = delivered)            -> yes/no
    - Within 30 days? (days_since_delivery <= 30) -> yes/no
    - Electronics and opened?                    -> yes/no
    Verdict: ELIGIBLE only if delivered = yes AND within 30 days = yes AND electronics-and-opened = no; otherwise NOT ELIGIBLE.
  Write the checks FIRST and the verdict LAST. Use days_since_delivery from the tool; never compute dates.
- Never invent orders, dates or amounts. If a tool returns ORDER_NOT_FOUND, say so.
- If no order ID is given, ask for it. Report statuses exactly as the tools return them.
- Politely decline questions unrelated to ShopEase.

parameters.toolDescription: Look up ONE order by order ID (e.g. ORD1024): item, category, status, delivery date, days_since_delivery, package_opened, courier tracking. lookup=ORDER_NOT_FOUND means it does not exist.
parameters.query:
SELECT q.requested AS order_id,
       CASE WHEN o.order_id IS NULL THEN 'ORDER_NOT_FOUND' ELSE 'FOUND' END AS lookup,
       o.item, o.category, o.amount_inr, o.status,
       CASE WHEN o.order_id IS NULL THEN NULL WHEN o.package_opened THEN 'yes' ELSE 'no' END AS package_opened,
       DATE_FORMAT(o.delivered_on, '%Y-%m-%d') AS delivered_on,
       DATEDIFF(CURDATE(), o.delivered_on)     AS days_since_delivery,
       o.courier, o.tracking_no
FROM (SELECT UPPER(TRIM($1)) AS requested) q
LEFT JOIN n8n.shop_orders o ON o.order_id = q.requested;

parameters.toolDescription: Look up a customer by customer ID (e.g. CUST01) or by one of their order IDs: name, city, loyalty tier.
parameters.query:
SELECT q.requested AS looked_up_by,
       CASE WHEN c.customer_id IS NULL THEN 'CUSTOMER_NOT_FOUND' ELSE 'FOUND' END AS lookup,
       c.customer_id, c.name, c.city, c.loyalty_tier
FROM (SELECT UPPER(TRIM($1)) AS requested) q
LEFT JOIN n8n.shop_customers c
       ON c.customer_id = q.requested
       OR c.customer_id = (SELECT customer_id FROM n8n.shop_orders WHERE order_id = q.requested);

options.queryReplacement: ={{ $fromAI('customer_or_order_id', `A customer ID like CUST01 or an order ID like ORD1024`, 'string') }}

parameters.toolDescription: Check whether a refund was requested for an order ID and its status (requested/approved/rejected/paid). lookup=NO_REFUND_REQUESTED means none exists.
parameters.query:
SELECT q.requested AS order_id,
       CASE WHEN o.order_id IS NULL THEN 'ORDER_NOT_FOUND'
            WHEN r.refund_id IS NULL THEN 'NO_REFUND_REQUESTED'
            ELSE 'REFUND_FOUND' END AS lookup,
       r.refund_id, r.reason, r.status AS refund_status, r.amount_inr
FROM (SELECT UPPER(TRIM($1)) AS requested) q
LEFT JOIN n8n.shop_orders o  ON o.order_id = q.requested
LEFT JOIN n8n.shop_refunds r ON r.order_id = q.requested;
